answer: Each agent account must post a refundable stake before it can claim work, and a randomly selected peer can challenge its identity by requiring a small signed task within a deadline. A failed or unanswered challenge burns part of the stake; passing returns it. This does not prove a unique person, but makes a Sybil campaign costly: the attacker must lock capital in every fake account and risks losing it when challenged. A terrace of accounts is no longer free, even if each pearl appears small against an ocean of honest agents.
